profile.headline: Mercenary for Hire (programming, not killing)
profile.summary:
http://district411.org/2016/11/20/faces-four-meet-jack-nguyen/

I write code and run my mouth for a living

positions.title: Software Contractor (Code Mercenary)
positions.description:
•	Developing iPhone/iPad Game

Currently developing iPhone/iPad game. Working Title: Bikini Commando. Adventure game for iPod Touch/iPhone/iPad built on iPhone SDK/Objective-C. This project combines diverse knowledge of multimedia tools (image editing, audio editing, animation) as well as story development. Demo: http://www.youtube.com/eviljack1234

•	ASP.NET site
Developed ASP.NET site for Orlando based insurance company. This site was built to allow third party vendors lookup current ticket status, print, view attachments. (Note: Link may be out of date soon)  Technlogies used: .NET/C#, SQL Server 2000

•	Developing adventure/racing game. 
Currently developing a role playing/racing game that is similar to transformers + tomb raider. So far I've integrated an open source physics engine (ODE - open dynamics engine, used in many military simulation projects) for collision detection with another open source rendering engine for graphics (OGRE - object oriented graphics rendering engine) and finally FMOD for sound. Demo: http://sites.google.com/site/eviljack/game-physics/frak 


•	Developed VOIP applications for social networking sites for startup VOIP company. Previous work includes developing applications that allow users to stream media to endpoint devices using in-house protocol, applying Fourier transforms to incoming audio for the purposes of lie detection. 

Technologies used: XML RPC, SOAP, VOIP, .NET, C#, C++, Fourier Transforms.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Lead Engineer for Biometric Security System

Was the lead developer for integrating fingerprint security system with company’s core product. This security system is in compliance US government TWIC initiative. This involved developing a windows client to enroll fingerprints from desktop fingerprint reader and storing that data and enrollment information in backend database. (Having a .NET client communicate with a QNX realtime OS over RPC). Project also encompassed having to integrate windows mobile security devices into security system. This project is a multi-million dollar project currently being pilot tested throughout the country. 

Technlogies used: .NET/ C#, windows mobile, QNX, Linux, C/C++, RPC, MySQL, SQL Server 2005 Express, microcontroller/PIC programming.


•	Primary developer for Event Report system

Developed a system that would log events throughout a facility (when someone in facility opens a gate, turns on a pump, leaves facility). This system would allow for reports and logs of activity and allow terminal operators to streamline their facility. Developed primarily in C/C++ on a linux platform.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Developed mobile phone app to allow webpage link based phone dialing

This application was a mobile version of one of Volo Communications core technologies. Based on one click of a button from a cell phone, a user could be connected to a contact’s cellphone or landline via Voice over IP technology. This application was created as a J2ME MIDlet which consumed a SOAP service that exposed our telephony APIs. Later this same application was ported to a mobile .NET site. Technlogies used: Java, J2ME, C#, .NET, asp.NET, SQL server, SOAP, XML

•	Developed a SIP softphone and embedded it inside of a webpage. (www.click4me.net/webphone) - Think Skype in a browser

Created a Skype clone that was runnable from inside any web browser. Users are able to go to any computer in the world and dial a US landline or cellphone for free. Technologies used: Java applets


•	Added Speex codec to our webphone. 

This provided dramatic improvement in overall call quality as the speex algorithm compressed the overall bandwidth required by an order of magnitude. Technologies used: Java applets, low level audio compression protocols


•	Created a Pirate Cell network. 

Leveraging the technologies available at Volo Communications we found numerous backdoors into all of the major cell carriers allowing us to make free calls, alter the calling number, and check other people’s voicemail. (Purely for research purposes. No malicious activities were done) Technologies used: ASP.NET, web services, java, SOAP, XML

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Ported Aplix “JBlend” Java Virtual Machine solution to Windows Mobile platform.

•	Worked extensively with various J2ME technologies, MIDlet creation, testing and debugging, some BREW work. Technologies used: C++, C, windows mobile 

•	Worked w/various wireless carrier Quality assurance testing systems (JDTS, Cingular, TCK)

•	Developed Serial Communication software over Bluetooth technology. Bluetooth technology allows for legacy applications to communicate over RS232 protocol.

•	Lead developer for enabling Bluetooth for Aplix Corp’s Java Virtual Machine. This specification is referred to as JSR 82. Technologies used: C++

•	Created installation toolkit software module. This toolkit allows engineers to convert text based files into proprietary file format.

•	Developed security protocol for OTA application installation. Developed system for installed applications to be verified through an encryption/decryption sequence. 

•	Promoted to Project Leader 5/2006

positions.title: Grraduate Lecturer / Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
•	Lecturing Teaching Assistant responsible for presentation of lectures to a group of 30 undergraduate students. Class: Introduction to Computer Science (CIS3020), a theoretical and mathematical foundation course. 

•	Taught discussion sections for CIS3020 (Introduction to Computer Science). Lectured on fundamental computer science and engineering concepts. 
 
•	Received the highest teacher evaluations from students among all of the Lecture Teaching Assistants in the U. of Florida for spring 2002 semester
